page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is an ARM-based compute-optimized server powered by 8 dedicated physical cores on the AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with an arm64 architecture, it features 16.0 GB of system memory, 32 MB of L3 cache, and 2 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The instance includes 474 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage.

Benchmark measurements show mid-range multi-threaded compute performance alongside steady web workload capabilities. The server records a stress-ng multi-core CPU result of 12133.14, a Geekbench multi-core score of 5364.0, and a software compilation score of 8140.0 using clang. In throughput evaluations, it achieves 9.43 million SET operations per second in Redis and 9.78 GB/sec in static web serving. Single-thread processing remains lower, evidenced by a single-core Geekbench score of 930.0 and a single-threaded bzip3 decompression output of 6.93 GB/sec.

The inclusion of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage alongside energy-efficient Graviton arm64 execution delivers solid resource density for applications needing low-latency local disk access without discrete graphics processing. While memory is limited to 2.0 GB per core, memory read bandwidth reaches 116.89 GB/sec on uncached 256MB blocks. These hardware properties position the c6gd.2xlarge for containerized services, build and compilation pipelines, memory caching tiers like Redis, and batch data tasks utilizing temporary local scratch space.
